decks.name: LeetCode #435 - Non-overlapping Intervals
decks.description: Find minimum number of intervals to remove to make rest non-overlapping

cards.question: Non-overlapping Intervals: Given an array of intervals intervals where intervals[i] = [starti, endi], return the minimum number of intervals you need to remove to make the rest of the intervals non-overlapping.

solutions.name: Recursion
solutions.explanation: Sort intervals first, then use recursion to try all possibilities. At each index, make two choices: skip current interval, or include it if non-overlapping with previous. Track previous interval index to check overlap. Base case when reaching end of array. Find maximum non-overlapping intervals that can be selected, then subtract from total to get removals. Explores all 2^n possibilities. Very inefficient without memoization. O(2^n) time complexity.

solutions.name: Dynamic Programming (Top-Down)
solutions.explanation: Optimize recursion with memoization. Sort by end time (greedy insight). Use DP to find maximum non-overlapping intervals. For each interval, try including it and recursively find max from remaining non-overlapping intervals. Memoize results to avoid recomputation. Check if next interval's start is after current's end. Return total intervals minus maximum non-overlapping to get removals. O(n^2) time with memoization avoiding exponential recalculation.

solutions.name: Dynamic Programming (Bottom-Up)
solutions.explanation: Iterative DP building solution bottom-up. Sort by end time. For each interval i, compute maximum non-overlapping intervals ending at i. Check all previous intervals j: if j's end <= i's start, can extend j's chain. Take maximum extension possible. Final answer is total minus maximum chain length found. Similar to Longest Increasing Subsequence pattern. O(n^2) time with O(n) space for DP array.

solutions.name: Dynamic Programming (Binary Search)
solutions.explanation: Optimize DP by using binary search to find last compatible interval. Sort by end time. For each interval, use binary search to find rightmost interval whose end <= current start. Either take previous DP value or extend found interval's chain. Binary search reduces finding compatible interval from O(n) to O(log n). Total O(n log n) time. Most efficient DP approach.

solutions.name: Greedy (Sort By Start)
solutions.explanation: Greedy approach sorting by start time. Track previous interval's end. For each interval: if starts after previous ends, update end to current. If overlaps, increment removal counter and keep interval with earlier end (better for future intervals). Greedy choice: always prefer interval ending earlier. Simple and efficient. O(n log n) time from sorting. Most practical solution.

solutions.name: Greedy (Sort By End)
solutions.explanation: Optimal greedy solution sorting by end time. Always select interval ending earliest. Track previous end time. For each interval: if starts before previous ends (overlap), increment removal counter but don't update end. If non-overlapping, update previous end. Key insight: sorting by end time ensures we always make optimal choice. Simpler than sort by start. O(n log n) time. Classic interval scheduling algorithm.
